objectives.text: Hold the regime through the national elections set for 22 December 2026. The first vice president, Riek Machar, has been on trial for treason in Juba since 22 September 2025, and the vote has been put off before: the last move (September 2024) pushed it from December 2024 to December 2026.

paradoxes.text: Removing the rival removes the peace the regime needs. The treason trial takes out the one figure who could contest the 2026 vote, but UN experts said in December 2025 that it is further eroding the 2018 agreement, the frame under which the UN mission and donors deal with Juba.

grand_strategy.reading: Juba's survival strategy is to keep the army and the oil revenue under one roof, remove the one rival able to contest the December 2026 vote, and buy protection with Ugandan troops and Emirati credit rather than with a settlement. Its weak point is the single pipe: every barrel crosses a Sudanese war in which South Sudan has no say, so the oil that keeps the state alive is also the lever Khartoum and the RSF hold. The 2018 agreement survives only as the diplomatic frame donors still use, and each move against Machar wears it down further.

stances.note: Uganda put special forces into Juba in March 2025: Kampala said the UPDF deployed to save Kiir and Juba, and Juba acknowledged technical and support units under a pre-existing military pact (a tier 4 pointer). No alliance treaty was found, so the grade is de facto alignment. No source uses the word ally: the grade is our reading of the structure (C). Bond affinity is our reading too; no source names it.

stances_toward.note: A relationship of mutual hostage: South Sudan's crude exits through Sudanese pipelines to Port Sudan, so Juba protects Heglig (SSPDF deployed 10 Dec 2025 under a Kiir-Burhan-Hemedti tripartite arrangement, after about 3,900 Sudanese soldiers crossed and were disarmed) and brokers with both camps, while the RSF-SPLM-N alliance on the border and the contested status of Heglig and Abyei keep the old war alive. Partner (transactional, no alignment) because both sides need the pipeline; Juba also signs with the RSF, so it is not an ally. Bond grievance: the 2011 secession, the 2012 Heglig war, Abyei.
